newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia reiterates Burma's right to join ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia reiterates Burma's right to join ASEAN.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi on Tuesday reiterated Malaysia's belief that Burma has a right to join ASEAN, but said the timing of the membership was still not decided.

"ASEAN (the Association of Southeast Asian Nations) has agreed that in the near future it will have 10 member nations and Myanmar (Burma) will be one of them. That is our policy," Abdullah told reporters.
"The question is when Myanmar would join ASEAN and that is secondary," he said.

ASEAN comprises Brunei, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma is already an observer in the group and is scheduled to become a full member by next year, with Laos and Cambodia to follow.

Abdullah was responding to questions on whether he would discuss Burma's entry into ASEAN with Rangoon's military government when he visits the state next week during an eight-day trip through Indochina, which includes stops in Vietnam and Cambodia.

He was also asked whether he would seek a clarification from Philippine President Fidel Ramos, who said recently that ASEAN might want to review its constructive engagement policy with Burma following moves by Rangoon to crack down on democratic forces in the country.

Most recently, the Rangoon government cut off the road to dissident Aung San Suu Kyi's house from September 26 to October 8 to stop her National League for Democracy (NLD) from holding a party congress.
The government also arrested 573 NLD party activists but later released them in stages.
"I've no plans to clarify anything to the Myanmar government on its ASEAN membership as our position is clear," Abdullah said.
"As for President Ramos, he'll be meeting other ASEAN leaders at an ASEAN summit this year and he can clarify his position if they didn't understand him," Abdullah added.
Top diplomats from ASEAN are due to meet in Kuala Lumpur on Friday and Saturday to discuss a host of administrative matters and Abdullah said the agenda would also include Burma.
"But it'll be on how we can familiarise Burma with ASEAN's ways, mannerisms and workings," he said.
